cd35ecc70496e16a5ef7cfb0075d17496e4ce7da.defense: Original A4 says switching costs exceed alternative gains after critical mass. If this includes coordinated switches, it can exclude the critics' profitable-return examples. A derivative-only example therefore does not refute every reading of all v2 premises.
cd35ecc70496e16a5ef7cfb0075d17496e4ce7da.objection: The old proof never quantifies that coalitional scope. Indeed if every returner gains at r=p-a(C), each re-entrant at r+a(B)<=p receives uE_i(r+a(B))<=uE_i(p)<uS_i(r). The profitable return is strong Nash in its reduced game. The old claimed profitable breakaway cannot follow.
cd35ecc70496e16a5ef7cfb0075d17496e4ce7da.resolution: Preserve A4 verbatim; state NR as explicit additional payoff content: every C of current Exit holders contains i with uE_i(p)>=uS_i(p-a(C)). The return lemma makes this exactly return resistance. At the greatest Nash profile, monotone best-response iteration excludes profitable entry-only deviations; any profitable combined entry/return deviation would imply a profitable return alone. Thus NR implies strong Nash and BPW.
cd35ecc70496e16a5ef7cfb0075d17496e4ce7da.new_hypothesis: NR is substantive and maintained, not derived from M1-M4, P1-P7, source citations or model agreement.
cd35ecc70496e16a5ef7cfb0075d17496e4ce7da.source_role: Sources supply definitions and established theorems; the displayed deduction applies them to this manuscript. No cited author is represented as having reviewed this paper.
